REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 13, 2020 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

This section is reserved for comments related to Consent Calendar Items and items not listed on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council/Successor Agency. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

Agenda Report

10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.
Closed Session
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
FEBRUARY 13, 2020, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin T. Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Division Youth Basketball
  League Rookie III Division team - Raptors.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager introduced Minh G. Dinh as the new captain of the
  Cerritos Sheriff's Station.

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer presented an informational update on the Tuesday,
  March 3, 2020 Cerritos General Municipal Election. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding a Neighborhood Watch meeting and Town Hall meetings.
  He submitted documents for the record (The documents are public record and full-
  text copies can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer).

  Norma Williamson thanked the City Council for their unanimous vote to ban the
  City’s use of the Roundup herbicide.

  Linda J. Hernandez thanked the City Council for their unanimous vote to ban the
  City’s use of the Roundup herbicide.

  Mary Ann Tipton thanked the City Council for their unanimous vote to ban the City’s
  use of the Roundup herbicide.

  Diana Needham thanked the City Council for their unanimous vote to ban the City’s
  use of the Roundup herbicide.

  Saul R. Lozada spoke regarding a recent Property Preservation Commission Meeting.
 City of Cerritos  February 13, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

6.  Public Comments (continued)

  Case Van der Linden spoke regarding traffic accidents in the City.

  Jay Gray spoke in opposition to the Measure C proposition on the ballot and inquired
  regarding allowing students to rehearse at the Cerritos Center for the Performing
  Arts.

  Sam Desai thanked the City Council for their service and spoke regarding the
  upcoming budget process and election.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of
  January 27, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of January 27, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 13, 2020
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands, as follows:

  City of Cerritos  2/13/2020  $6,027,644.94 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated February 13, 2020 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands as follows:

  Successor Agency  2/13/2020  $17,500.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)
 City of Cerritos  February 13, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.2. (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period
  ending December 31, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending December 31,
  2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO DE-CLASSIFY A SEGMENT OF SHOEMAKER AVENUE AS A DESIGNATED
  TRUCK ROUTE (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Management Analyst. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Faye Ashby thanked the City for their recent actions to mitigate truck traffic on
  Bloomfield Avenue and requested the City remain vigilant regarding continued truck
  and traffic enforcement.

  Mel Cortez spoke in support of the proposed ordinance.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to waive full
  reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1031, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE
  TO DE-CLASSIFY A SEGMENT OF SHOEMAKER AVENUE AS A DESIGNATED
  TRUCK ROUTE (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  February 13, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration to commence the required biennial review of the City’s
  Conflict of Interest Codes pursuant to the California Political Reform Act of 1974
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Hu, to direct the City
  Clerk/Treasurer to:

  1. Commence the biennial review by notifying each City agency (City, Successor
  Agency, and Financing Authority) to begin reviewing each of their codes; and

  2. Report back to the City Council with a notice of anticipated changes no later than the
  final City Council/Successor Agency meeting of September, 2020; and

  3. Present any proposed changes to the codes for review and adoption no later than the
  final City Council/Successor Agency meeting of December, 2020 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an award of a contract for supply and delivery of
  compressed liquid chlorine, Bid No. 1395-20 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Management Analyst.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award an annual contract for the supply of compressed liquid chlorine, Bid No. 1395-
  20, to JCI Jones Chemicals, Inc. of Torrance, California and reject all other bids; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract-related change
  orders required to ensure the supply and delivery of compressed liquid chlorine for
  the provision of safe drinking water (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  February 13, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Pulido, Mayor Pro Tem
  Yokoyama, and Mayor Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Directed staff to conduct a study on the potential ban of
  straws and single-use plastics.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:30 p.m. in memory of Fred Humphrey.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
